paper_title: The Role of Model Architecture and Scale in Predicting Molecular   Properties Insights from Fine-Tuning RoBERTa, BART, and LLaMA
caption: Training Loss vs. Steps for Each Model Type by Model Size with a Data Size of 20 millions. The loss trends for 10 million and 20 million datasets are similar.
model_annotation: This plot illustrates the training loss over training steps for six model configurations trained on a 20 million data size, titled "Training Loss of 20M Data Size." The x-axis represents the training step, labeled "Step," displayed on a linear scale with tick marks at 0K, 20K, 40K, 60K, and 80K in the main panel, with a broken axis revealing a continuation from approximately 420K to 440K on the right side. The y-axis represents "Train Loss" on a linear scale ranging from 0.0 to 0.85, with tick marks at intervals of approximately 0.05 to 0.1. Six lines are shown, each corresponding to a different model configuration: ChemBART Small 20M (red, solid), ChemBART Medium 20M (blue, solid), ChemBERTa Small 20M (green, solid), ChemBERTa Medium 20M (orange, solid), ChemLLaMA Small 20M (purple, solid), and ChemLLaMA Medium 20M (brown, solid). All six lines begin at high training loss values near 0.75–0.80 at the earliest steps and exhibit a steep decline during the first approximately 10K steps, dropping to roughly 0.2–0.35. After this initial rapid decrease, all lines continue to decline more gradually through the remainder of the main panel up to around 80K steps. The ChemBERTa Small 20M (green) and ChemBERTa Medium 20M (orange) lines tend to remain at somewhat higher loss values compared to the others, settling around 0.15–0.19 by 80K steps. The ChemLLaMA Small 20M (purple) line appears to reach among the lowest values, descending to approximately 0.05–0.08 by 80K steps. The ChemBART Small (red) and ChemBART Medium (blue) lines follow intermediate trajectories, reaching approximately 0.08–0.12 by 80K steps. The ChemLLaMA Medium 20M (brown) line settles around 0.10–0.15 in the later portion of the main panel. In the broken-axis continuation from 420K to 440K, the lines appear to have largely stabilized, with ChemLLaMA Small 20M (purple) at approximately 0.02–0.03, ChemBART variants around 0.03–0.05, ChemLLaMA Medium around 0.04–0.06, and ChemBERTa variants at approximately 0.08–0.12, all showing relatively flat behavior with minor fluctuations. No markers are used on any of the lines.
